meta.title: About us
meta.description: Meet Meridian Partners: an independent advisory firm with offices in Shanghai, Moscow and Dubai and 18 years of cross-border experience.

hero.title: Independent advisors for companies crossing borders
hero.lead: Founded in Shanghai in 2008, Meridian Partners now supports clients from three regional offices with a team of consultants, analysts and former industry executives.

story.title: Built where the work happens
paragraphs: Meridian began with a simple observation: companies expanding between Asia, Eurasia and the Gulf were receiving advice written far from the markets themselves. Strategies looked sound on paper but stalled at the first licence application or partner meeting.

So we built the firm the other way round. Our consultants live and work in the markets they advise on, speak the languages of their counterparts and have run operations themselves. That local depth is combined with one shared methodology, so clients get consistent quality wherever they expand.
Today we advise industrial groups, investors and fast-growing technology firms, and we remain independent: we accept no commissions from the partners, distributors or service providers we recommend.

insights.author: Chen Ruoxi
insights.title: Setting up in China: four questions to answer before you register a company
insights.excerpt: A local entity unlocks contracts, hiring and invoicing in China — but only if the structure matches your business model. These are the questions we ask every client first.

body.heading: Do you need an entity at all?
paragraphs: Many companies test the market through a distributor or a cross-border e-commerce channel before committing capital. If your first year is about validating demand, a well-chosen partner can be faster and cheaper than a company of your own. An entity becomes essential once you need to sign contracts locally, employ staff directly or issue official tax invoices (fapiao) to customers.

body.heading: Which structure, and which city?
paragraphs: Most foreign investors choose a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company, while joint ventures remain common in regulated sectors or when a partner brings licences and relationships. Location matters as much as structure: Shanghai, Shenzhen and Chengdu offer different incentives, talent pools and proximity to customers, and local authorities differ in how quickly they process applications.

body.heading: How much capital, and when?
paragraphs: Since China's revised Company Law took effect in July 2024, subscribed capital in a limited liability company generally has to be paid in within five years. Set registered capital to reflect a realistic budget for the first years of operation rather than an impressive headline figure.

body.heading: What else belongs in the plan?
paragraphs: Allow time for opening a bank account, tax registration and social insurance enrolment, and plan early for data rules: if you will transfer personal information out of China, the Personal Information Protection Law may require additional steps. Finally, draft partner and employment contracts on the assumption that disputes will be heard by Chinese courts or arbitration bodies.

insights.author: Elena Sokolova
insights.title: EAC certification: a practical roadmap for exporters to the Eurasian Economic Union
insights.excerpt: One conformity mark opens five markets, but the process rewards preparation. Here is how to plan certification without delaying your launch.

body.heading: One mark, five markets
paragraphs: Products covered by the Eurasian Economic Union's technical regulations must carry the EAC mark before they can be sold in Russia, Kazakhstan, Belarus, Armenia or Kyrgyzstan. The good news is that a single certificate or declaration of conformity is valid in all five countries.

body.heading: Start with classification
paragraphs: The first step is to identify which technical regulations apply to your product: machinery safety, low-voltage equipment, electromagnetic compatibility and food-contact materials are common combinations. The applicable regulations determine whether you need a certificate issued by an accredited body or a declaration of conformity registered by the applicant.

body.heading: Appoint a local applicant
paragraphs: Certificates and declarations are issued to an applicant registered in an EAEU member state — typically your subsidiary, your importer or an authorised representative. Choose this partner carefully: they carry legal responsibility for the documents and often keep control of them if the relationship ends.

body.heading: Plan testing and labelling early
paragraphs: Testing must be carried out by laboratories accredited within the Union, and technical documentation and labelling must be available in Russian. For most industrial products, a well-prepared file can move from application to approval in a few weeks; incomplete technical documentation is the most common cause of delay. Above all, first confirm that the product and your counterparties are not restricted by the sanctions or export-control rules that apply to your company.

insights.author: Omar Al-Hashimi
insights.title: Riyadh or Dubai? Choosing a regional headquarters in the Gulf
insights.excerpt: The decision is no longer only about lifestyle and connectivity. Government contracts, tax and talent now point in different directions.

body.heading: Why the question has changed
paragraphs: For two decades, Dubai was the default base for regional operations. Saudi Arabia's regional headquarters programme has changed the calculation: companies that want to contract with Saudi government entities are now generally expected to have a regional headquarters in the Kingdom.

body.heading: What Dubai still offers
paragraphs: The UAE combines world-class connectivity, established free zones and a deep pool of international talent. Since federal corporate tax was introduced in 2023, qualifying free-zone companies can still benefit from preferential rates, but the rules reward genuine substance rather than a registered address.

body.heading: What Riyadh offers
paragraphs: Saudi Arabia is the largest economy in the GCC, and its investment programmes span energy, infrastructure, tourism and manufacturing. Licensed regional headquarters can access tax incentives and support with visas and hiring, in exchange for meeting substance requirements such as a minimum number of senior staff.

body.heading: Making the choice
paragraphs: Start from your customers rather than the incentives. If Saudi government or giga-project contracts are central to your plan, a Riyadh headquarters is probably unavoidable, and many groups keep a commercial or logistics hub in Dubai as well. We usually recommend modelling both options over five years, including people, tax and the cost of running two locations.

insights.author: Chen Ruoxi
insights.title: One website, three search ecosystems: localizing for Baidu, Yandex and Arabic search
insights.excerpt: Translation is only the start. Hosting, page speed and local platforms decide whether customers in China, Russia and the Gulf ever find your site.

body.heading: China: speed and hosting come first
paragraphs: Many Google services, including Google Fonts, Maps and reCAPTCHA, are blocked or unreliable in Mainland China, and a single blocked script can leave a page loading for seconds. Self-host fonts and scripts, keep pages light and, if you host inside the mainland, complete the ICP filing required for locally hosted websites.

body.heading: Russia: Yandex rewards local relevance
paragraphs: Yandex remains the leading search engine in Russia. Register the site in Yandex Webmaster, set the target region and write Russian content for Russian readers rather than translating word for word. A clear structure, fast pages and accurate hreflang tags help both Yandex and Google.

body.heading: The Gulf: Arabic first, right to left
paragraphs: Google dominates search in the GCC, but audiences increasingly expect native Arabic content. That means a true right-to-left layout — mirrored navigation, icons and forms — and copy written by Arabic speakers, with English kept for international partners.

body.heading: Build once, publish everywhere
paragraphs: A single codebase with a structured content model keeps every language in sync. Static pages served from a CDN with nodes close to each audience deliver the speed that every search engine rewards.
